pharm: Orally administered ester prodrug of ampicillin rapidly hydrolyzed by plasma esterases to active ampicillin; better and more complete oral absorption than ampicillin, allowing twice-daily dosing.
quick: May be taken with or without food
Small amounts in milk; generally compatible with caution
Reduce dose/extend interval in significant impairment
summary: Bacampicillin is the 1-ethoxycarbonyloxyethyl ester prodrug of ampicillin. It has no intrinsic antibacterial activity but is rapidly hydrolyzed after oral absorption to ampicillin, an aminopenicillin bactericidal against many Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms. Improved oral absorption permits twice-daily dosing. It is no longer marketed or FDA-approved in the United States (Spectrobid discontinued); information here reflects historical labeling and SmPC/BNF-type sources.
indications: Upper and lower respiratory tract infections (e.g., tonsillitis, bronchitis, pneumonia) due to susceptible organisms
Urinary tract infections due to susceptible organisms

dosage.n: Each mg bacampicillin yields ~0.62-0.73 mg ampicillin; dosing as ampicillin equivalent
Adjust by infection severity; not for neonates
Ampicillin is renally cleared; adjust in significant impairment

admin: Take by mouth with or without food (absorption is less affected by food than ampicillin)
Swallow tablets whole with water; pediatric suspension where available
Complete the full prescribed course even if symptoms resolve
moa: Prodrug hydrolyzed by plasma esterases to ampicillin, which binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits bacterial cell wall (peptidoglycan) synthesis, producing bactericidal activity against susceptible Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms. It is susceptible to beta-lactamase hydrolysis.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to penicillins or any beta-lactam
History of severe reaction (anaphylaxis) to a beta-lactam

preg: Penicillins, including ampicillin, are generally regarded as acceptable in pregnancy when indicated; use if benefit justifies use.
lact: Ampicillin is excreted in breast milk in small amounts; generally considered compatible with breastfeeding, with caution for infant sensitization, rash, or diarrhea.
renal: Ampicillin is primarily renally eliminated; reduce dose or extend the dosing interval in significant renal impairment.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment generally required; monitor in prolonged therapy.

moderate: Probenecid (reduces renal excretion, increasing ampicillin levels)
Oral combined contraceptives (possible reduced efficacy - advise additional precautions)
minor: Bacteriostatic antibiotics (e.g., tetracyclines, chloramphenicol) may antagonize bactericidal activity
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urinary glucose with copper-reduction (Clinitest) methods; can affect estriol assays in pregnancy.

monitoring: Signs of hypersensitivity, especially after the first dose
Renal, hepatic, and hematologic parameters during prolonged therapy
counsel: Complete the full course even if you feel better
Report any rash, itching, swelling, or difficulty breathing immediately
Tell your doctor of any penicillin or cephalosporin allergy
Seek care for severe or bloody diarrhea, which may occur during or after treatment
If you take oral contraceptives, use additional contraceptive precautions during and shortly after the course
pk: Rapidly hydrolyzed to ampicillin after absorption
Ampicillin peak ~0.5-1 hour after oral dose
Effective plasma levels sustained, supporting q12h dosing
Store in a cool, dry place per label; reconstituted suspension refrigerate and discard per labeling
pearls: NOTE: Not FDA-approved/marketed in the US (Spectrobid discontinued); this record reflects historical labeling and SmPC/BNF-type sources
Inactive prodrug - antibacterial effect is entirely due to ampicillin released after absorption
Better oral bioavailability than ampicillin, allowing twice-daily rather than four-times-daily dosing
Causes a high rate of rash in patients with infectious mononucleosis - avoid
Beta-lactamase susceptible - not active against many resistant Gram-negatives
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Overdose may cause GI upset and, with very high levels or renal impairment, neurotoxicity (seizures). Manage supportively; ampicillin is removed by hemodialysis. Maintain hydration and monitor renal/neurologic status.
